extracted.intended_audience: interested members of the public and stakeholders (including commercial surfclam and ocean quahog industry), fishery managers, and other commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for members of the public and stakeholders to submit timely, properly identified comments on NOAA's Amendment 21 (Species Separation Requirements Amendment) to the Atlantic Surfclam and Ocean Quahog Fishery Management Plan, including where to obtain supporting documents and how comments will be handled. Also describes the proposed measures and statutory limits relevant to the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received on or before February 27, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered, comments must be received by close of business on the last day of the comment period. Comments received after that date will not be considered in the decision to approve or disapprove Amendment 21, including those postmarked or otherwise transmitted by the last day of the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit comments via the Federal e-Rulemaking Portal (Regulations.gov) or by mail to the Regional Administrator at the Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic Submission: go to https://www.regulations.gov and enter NOAA-NMFS-2025-1197 in the Search box, click the 'Comment' icon, complete required fields, and enter or attach comments. Mail: submit written comments to Michael Pentony, Regional Administrator, NMFS, Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office, 55 Great Republic Drive, Gloucester, MA 01930, and mark the outside of the envelope: 'Comments on Surfclam/Ocean Quahog Amendment 21.' Comments sent by any other method, to any other address or individual, or received after the end of the comment period, may not be considered by NMFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket identification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be identified by NOAA-NMFS-2025-1197 (and the associated Document ID) when submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entering the docket number in Regulations.gov search box directs commenters to the correct submission form; mailing instructions specify marking the envelope with the comment subject to ensure proper docketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record and availability of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received are a part of the public record and will generally be posted for public viewing on www.regulations.gov without change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies review submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and personally identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: NMFS will accept anonymous comments; however, personal identifying information or confidential business information submitted voluntarily will be publicly accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To remain anonymous, enter 'N/A' in the required fields on Regulations.gov. Be aware that voluntarily submitted personal identifying or sensitive business information may appear in the public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of amendment documents and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of Amendment 21, including the draft Environmental Assessment (EA), are available on request from the Mid-Atlantic Fishery Management Council and accessible online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request copies from the Mid-Atlantic Fishery Management Council, 800 North State Street, Suite 201, Dover, DE 19901, or visit https://www.mafmc.org. The Federal Register PDF linked in the document sidebar is the official electronic format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of comments for decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments received by the close of the comment period will be considered in the approval/disapproval decision on the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late comments (received after the close of business on the last day) will not be considered in that approval/disapproval decision. If the amendment is approved, a subsequent proposed rule will be published with another opportunity for public comment on specific regulatory changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive amendment measures described (policy elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment 21 would allow vessels to land both surfclams and ocean quahogs on the same fishing trip, with landed catch sorted at the dealer's processing facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures approved by the Council include changing species separation rules to permit mixed-species landings and shifting sorting responsibility to dealer facilities to reflect the practical difficulty of sorting aboard industrial dredge vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and observer coverage requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment 21 calls for the creation of a new monitoring program within dealer processing facilities and additional at-sea observer coverage up to an initial target coverage of 5 percent of all clam dredge fishing trips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monitoring program is intended to ensure accurate accounting for catch, including landings and discards of both species under the ITQ system. The initial at-sea observer coverage target is specified as up to 5 percent of trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry cost recovery and fee limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional monitoring would be funded by the industry through cost recovery; the Magnuson-Stevens Act authorizes a fee to recover actual costs related to management, data collection, and enforcement of limited access privilege programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee collected to recover monitoring/management costs cannot exceed three percent of the ex-vessel value of the fish harvested under the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact for further information
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information, contact Douglas Potts, Fishery Policy Analyst, 978-281-9341.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided contact for substantive or procedural questions about Amendment 21 or the associated documents.
